Re: Appeal of denial for rotator cuff repair  
Member: Riley Kimura  
Member ID: W548803729  
Reference number: POC-F4D8086686-78032  
Requested procedure: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827  
Plan: Avera Health Plans Commercial/ACA, South Dakota  

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Avera Health Plans’ denial of prior authorization for rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827. The denial states that the imaging submitted did not support medical necessity. The plan has not provided me with the specific medical policy or clinical-review criteria applied to this request, so this appeal does not quote or rely on any unpublished plan policy language.

The submitted records support the requested procedure:

- MRI performed on July 11, 2026, shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not resolved with rest.
- I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, including 16 visits from April 10, 2026, through July 3, 2026. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 22, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- My condition substantially limits function. I cannot lift the affected arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance use. I am a nonsmoker, and my BMI is 29.
- The procedure was requested by Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery.

The MRI does not merely show nonspecific shoulder pain. It documents a structural full-thickness tear of the supraspinatus with associated fatty atrophy. The imaging findings are consistent with the persistent symptoms, objective examination findings, functional limitations, and failure of an extensive course of conservative treatment. The limited and temporary response to injection further supports that nonoperative treatment has not adequately resolved the condition.

Please overturn the denial and approve CPT 29827. If Avera Health Plans maintains the denial, please provide the exact medical policy or clinical-review criteria used, including the policy title, policy number, version or effective date, the specific imaging requirements, and the clinical rationale for concluding that the July 11, 2026 MRI did not satisfy those criteria. Please also identify any additional information required for approval and provide the opportunity for Reyes, MD, to discuss the case with the reviewing clinician.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Riley Kimura
